title: Higgs Fluctuation Solver in Four Dimensions: Part II-Toward Finite Lattice-to-MS bar Matching in the SU(2) Higgs Extension
summary: We present a lattice-to-MS_bar matching framework for the $SU(2)$-Higgs theory, including Wilson-plaquette and fundamental scalar-link actions, a counter term basis through $ρ^{12}$, audited momentum-dependent lattice vertices, and fixed routings and projectors. At the benchmark $a=0.8$, $m_0^2=μ_R^2=0.4$, $g_0=0.65$, and $(λ,γ,δ)=(-2,0.8,0.08)$, the potential is $V_0(ρ)=\frac{1}{5}ρ^2-\frac{1}{2}ρ^4+\frac{2}{15}ρ^6+\frac{1}{100}ρ^8$. The scalar-only radial matching shifts, ordered as $(δm^2,δλ,δγ,δδ,δc_{10},δc_{12})$, are $(2.75293, -1.45119, -2.85120, 0.356724, 1.07432, 6.20492)$ in solver units, with the continuum-renormalized-minus-lattice convention. The Higgs two-point slope gives $δZ_H = 0.0329117974 \pm 0.00000036$ (QMC error). We also evaluate gauge-linked four-, six-, and eight-Higgs projections and derive the continuum one-loop gauge two-point tensor. The tensor passes 29 internal checks; at $p^2=0.4$, its total transverse projection is $Π_T=-0.01847$ at zero regulator and $-0.01716$ at $λ_{\mathrm{IR}}/μ_R=1/8$, while the regulator-induced longitudinal projection is $Π_L=1.04\times 10^{-5}$ at $λ_{\mathrm{IR}}/μ_R=1/32$. These results establish a tested foundation and quantitative benchmarks for the matching program. The gauge-linked projections remain preliminary, and full gauge-sector matching and Ward-Slavnov-Taylor closure are needed before a matched $SU(2)$ decay prefactor can be claimed.

title: Optimized solver algorithms for computing $\mathrm{Tr}(A^{-1})$
comment: 9 pages, 5 figures. To be published in the proceedings of LATTICE 2026
summary: Estimating the trace of the inverse of a large quark matrix is a longstanding problem in lattice QCD. The standard approach is Hutchinson's method, which uses random noise vectors to estimate the trace to a desired statistical tolerance. Each noise vector $b$ requires solving a system of linear equations $Ax = b$. In this work, we introduce a new class of Krylov solvers for this task, called Twin methods. Twin methods generate the Krylov polynomial once then reuse it on all other right-hand sides. This reduces the number of basic linear algebra operations in the algorithm and therefore lowers the trace computation time. We apply the Twin approach to BiCG and BiCGStab and test them on lattice QCD matrices of varying size and in a range of computing contexts. We also present a more economical estimation of $\mathrm{Tr}(A^{-1})$ which implements a polynomial approximation of $A^{-1}$ and a singular value deflation. In this scheme, the solvers are applied to only a few noise vectors, and the remainder are treated by the polynomial and the deflation. In our tests, the polynomial approximation combined with the deflation yield a 17-fold speedup in the time required to compute the trace over standard Hutchinson's method.

title: Numerical tests of 5D APS $η$-invariant phases for 4D chiral fermions
summary: We calculate the phase of a 4D chiral fermion determinant from the 5D Atiyah--Patodi--Singer (APS) $η$-invariant. We study the anomaly-free $SU(5)$ representation $\mathbf{10}\oplus\overline{\mathbf 5}$ on a four-torus, using gauge fields independent of one coordinate. For these backgrounds, the 4D phase can be calculated independently from a 3D Dirac spectrum. For an Abelian background embedded in $SU(5)$, two different 5D bulk extensions reproduce the 4D phase within $0.03\%$ in the tested heat-kernel extrapolations. One extension changes the spatial gauge field along the fifth direction and requires a coupled 5D spectral calculation. An independent single-charge check reproduces the Chern--Simons anomaly coefficient within $0.3\%$ using quadratic extrapolations. We also calculate 5D APS phases for non-Abelian backgrounds in the $SU(4)\times U(1)$ subgroup. For a background generating the full $\mathfrak{su}(4)$ algebra, the 5D phase with a fixed spatial field agrees with the independent 4D phase within $0.5\%$ over the six heat-kernel parameters examined. We further study a varying-field 5D extension for an embedded $SU(2)$ background. These results show that the 5D APS calculation reproduces a nonzero chiral phase after anomaly cancellation.

title: From Resonance Properties to High-Energy Behavior: The $R$ Ratio from Lattice QCD
summary: We investigate resonance properties and inclusive spectral behavior through Bayesian reconstruction of the $R$-ratio from Euclidean lattice correlators near the physical pion mass. Without additional Gaussian smearing, the reconstructed spectrum already captures the smooth high-energy behavior observed in experiment. Direct integration of the $ρ$ peak determines $f_ρ$ with approximately $1\%$ statistical precision and close agreement with the experimental reference, providing access to resonance properties without resolving individual finite-volume levels. With a common Gaussian width of $σ=0.6$~GeV, the lattice and experimental $R$-ratios show good overall agreement over $0.25$--$2.50$~GeV. Comparisons among ensembles with spatial extents up to approximately $10$~fm demonstrate that finite-volume effects can be controlled across these complementary observables. These results demonstrate a unified framework for studying resonance and inclusive physics from lattice QCD, with potential applications to other hadronic channels, inclusive decay rates, and hadronic tensors.

title: Solving fermionic sign problems with physics-informed kernels
summary: We extend the generative sampling approach with physics-informed kernels (PIKs) [1,2] to a general class of physics systems with complex distributions and a structure also encountered in fermionic systems. The resolution of sign problems of generic weighted sums of complex Gaußian distributions with the PIK approach is central to this application. In a first step, PIKs map a real normal distribution to such a weighted sum, and this procedure is called the PIKfan. The PIKfan has the sampling cost of a real normal distribution. In a second step, this weighted sum is evolved with a second PIK into the distribution of the theory at hand. In combination, we reduce the sampling task for a general class of complex systems to a Gaußian one, and the main computational task is that of computing the PIK. We illustrate the approach with the one-site Hubbard model at arbitrary chemical potential and with $φ^4$-deformed extensions of it.

title: Sampling non-abelian lattice gauge theories with diffusion models
comment: 7 pages, 4 figures, contribution to the Proceedings of the 22nd International Conference on QCD in Extreme Conditions (xQCD 2026), 14-17 July 2026, Busan, Korea
summary: We present gauge-equivariant diffusion models as samplers for lattice gauge theories (LGTs). Using lattice gauge-equivariant convolutional neural networks (L-CNNs) and the Metropolis-adjusted annealed Langevin algorithm (MAALA), we are able to accurately sample two-dimensional U(2) field configurations and show first promising results for four-dimensional SU(3). Our two-dimensional models extrapolate remarkably well to larger inverse couplings than originally trained on. We confirm this by comparing observables to analytically known values and to hybrid Monte Carlo results.
